➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

Want to become an AI Engineer in 2026?

Don't start with LangChain.
Don't start with Pinecone.
Don't even start with AI Agents.
Start by understanding this roadmap. 👇

Most people jump straight into building AI apps.
They copy tutorials.
They connect APIs.
They launch chatbots.
But when something breaks...
They have no idea why.
Because they skipped the fundamentals.
Here's the AI ecosystem every aspiring AI Engineer should understand.

🧠 1. LLMs – The Brain
These power reasoning, coding, conversations, and content generation.
Examples:
• GPT
• Claude
• Gemini
• Llama 4
• Qwen 3
• DeepSeek
• Mistral
• Gemma 3
• Phi-4
👉 Learn what each model is good at and when to use it.

⚡ 2. Frameworks – The Orchestrator
Frameworks connect LLMs with tools, APIs, memory, and workflows.
Popular choices:
• LangChain
• LlamaIndex
• Haystack
• txtai
👉 These help you build production-ready AI applications.

📚 3. Vector Databases – AI Memory
LLMs don't remember your documents.
Vector databases do.
Popular options:
• Pinecone
• Chroma
• Qdrant
• Weaviate
• Milvus
• PostgreSQL (pgvector)
• Cassandra
• OpenSearch
👉 Essential for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

📄 4. Data Extraction – Feed Your AI
Before AI can answer questions...
It needs clean, structured data.
Tools include:
• Crawl4AI
• FireCrawl
• ScrapeGraphAI
• MegaParser
• Docling
• LlamaParse
• ExtractThinker
👉 Great AI starts with great data.

🚀 5. Open LLM Access
Experiment, self-host, and deploy open-source models with:
• Hugging Face
• Ollama
• Groq
• Together AI
👉 Perfect for local development and production deployments.

🔍 6. Text Embeddings – The Search Engine
Embeddings convert text into vectors that AI can understand and retrieve.
Popular providers:
• OpenAI
• Voyage AI
• Google
• Cohere
• Nomic
• SBERT
👉 The quality of your embeddings directly impacts your RAG system.

📊 7. Evaluation – The Most Overlooked Layer
A good AI app isn't the one that looks smart.
It's the one that's measurably reliable.
Evaluate:
✅ Accuracy
✅ Hallucinations
✅ Retrieval quality
✅ Response consistency
Tools like Giskard and DeepEval help you build AI you can trust.

 If I were starting from scratch today, I'd learn in this order:
1️⃣ LLM Fundamentals
2️⃣ Prompt Engineering
3️⃣ Embeddings
4️⃣ Vector Databases
5️⃣ RAG
6️⃣ AI Frameworks
7️⃣ AI Agents
8️⃣ Evaluation
Master these, and you'll understand how modern AI systems are actually built.
Not just how to copy them.

One share could help a student, developer or job seeker understand the AI stack that companies are actually hiring for.

⚡️ President Pezeshkian warns against regional sabotage, stresses adherence to commitments for peace

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has warned that certain actors are actively attempting to destabilize the West Asia region and impede peace efforts, emphasizing that mutual respect and practical adherence to previous obligations are the essential prerequisites for any sustainable and successful diplomatic agreement.

President Pezeshkian made the remarks in a telephone conversation with Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday evening.
​
The phone call centered on the latest regional developments, the necessity of maintaining diplomatic momentum, and the shared commitment to securing sustainable peace.
​
During the conversation, President Pezeshkian addressed the security landscape of the region, noting that certain international actors are actively working to derail ongoing peace efforts. He specifically criticized the actions of the Israeli regime and the United States, saying that they are deviating from previous commitments and undermining stability.
​
The current situation requires a firm commitment to diplomatic channels to stabilize ceasefires and prevent the expansion of crises, President Pezeshkian stated. He emphasized that Iran has consistently acted in good faith, adhering to its obligations.
​
The president warned that for any agreement to be successful and lasting, mutual respect and practical adherence to commitments are non-negotiable prerequisites. He further clarified that Iran’s foreign policy decisions and negotiations are conducted within the framework of the state’s macro-policies, under the guidance and oversight of the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.
​
He also commended Pakistan’s constructive role in diplomatic efforts, specifically valuing the effective steps taken by Prime Minister Sharif and Army Chief General Asim Munir to de-escalate tensions and promote peaceful initiatives.
​
President Pezeshkian further acknowledged the strategic relationship between Tehran and Islamabad, deeply rooted in shared history, religion, and culture.
​
He expressed gratitude for the high-level Pakistani delegation that attended the funeral and commemoration of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, citing it as a testament to the enduring solidarity between the two nations.
​
Furthermore, he called for an acceleration in implementing existing economic agreements, urging responsible agencies to bolster cooperation in trade, agriculture, transportation, and industry to fully leverage mutual potential.
​
In response, Prime Minister Sharif reiterated the fraternal bond between the two countries, describing his nation’s participation in the recent memorial ceremonies as an essential duty. Expressing deep concern over the potential for renewed escalation in the region, he emphasized the urgent need for restraint and persistent political efforts to ensure a lasting ceasefire.
​
Pakistan remains fully prepared to continue its role in advancing diplomatic processes and de-escalating tensions, alongside other regional initiatives, including those led by Qatar, PM Sharif affirmed. He underscored Iran’s critical position in regional equations and expressed confidence that Tehran’s leadership would manage the current challenges with wisdom and prudence.
​
Both sides concluded the call by reaffirming their determination to maintain continuous political consultation and to rigorously pursue the implementation of bilateral economic and trade agreements.
